provenance.derivation: Editorial, anchored on boundaries the product already states (F-223, ADR-0102). LIGHTNESS is classified by the midpoint of the profile's lightness range — the statistic the profile screen already uses to name a band — against the phrase lexicon's measured gaps, 0.395 (dark|medium) and 0.725 (medium|light): the product's one definition of dark and light (ADR-0069), held by an agreement test against the published lexicon. CHROMA is classified by the midpoint of the chroma range against the lexicon's 0.039 and 0.100, for the same reason. TEMPERATURE is classified by the bias, at ±1/6: halfway between the values the guided derivation can reach (0 and ±1/3), because ADR-0069 §3 puts a boundary in a gap, never on a reachable value — and the derivation's own threshold, 1/3, is exactly such a value and treats a leans-warm and a leans-cool split differently in floating point (F-276). CONTRAST IS NOT READ: the convention drawn has no contrast axis, the photo path abstains on contrast, and it is the dimension established with the least direct evidence. THE TABLE encodes the structure of the twelve-season convention — warm light and warm deep are spring and autumn, cool light and cool deep are summer and winter, and in the middle of the lightness scale chroma decides bright or muted — and answers no summary wherever the convention needs a distinction the ranges do not make. NOTHING HERE IS MEASURED: the convention is a convention, not an instrument, and whether it or the derivation beneath it performs evenly across skin tones has not been studied (NFR-23, F-037).
provenance.editorialNotes: Reviewed by its own author (ADR-0060, OQ-5). What a second editor would most likely argue with: FIRST, a lightness range at an end of the scale outranks chroma, so a warm, light, low-chroma profile reads spring light rather than autumn muted — the convention's own charts disagree about that corner, and the choice is that the most visible characteristic names the label. SECOND, eleven of the twenty-seven cells answer no summary — every neutral temperature, and the two where lightness and chroma are both in the middle — so the convention's warm and cool "true" seasons are never named; naming them needs a distinction the ranges do not make. THIRD, "muted" has three definitions in this product: the lexicon's chroma regions (chosen here), the profile screen's chroma chips (ceilings 0.05, 0.1, 0.2), and this rule's word; they are written down together so the disagreement is found by reading rather than by a user. FOURTH, the Japanese words are katakana transliterations, not reviewed by a competent speaker. The rule reads no corpus value and names a colour's season nowhere: "autumn" here is a personal-colour type and unrelated to taxonomy.season.

axes.rationale: Warm, neutral or cool by the bias, split at ±1/6 — in the gap between the values a guided profile can reach (0 and ±1/3), so a two-of-three split lands the same way warm or cool, and a value exactly on a boundary is neutral on both sides.
Dark, medium or light by the midpoint of the lightness range, at the phrase lexicon's measured gaps — the product's one definition of dark and light (ADR-0069).
Low, moderate or high by the midpoint of the chroma range, at the phrase lexicon's measured gaps between authored chroma bands.
